title: Congruence
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you know when you are being true to yourself?
Jose asked: what are the signs that we are listening to our true selves? A student said: a flow state. Another said: when there is a lot of negativity or pessimism, that is when I am not.
Jose said: you are true to yourself when you are not dragging a negative belief system and an inner critic.
Jose asked what failure means. A student said: you either gave up in the process or you lost. Jose said: is there failure, or just process? It is process.
He said that when someone says I failed or I am not good at that, ask where that is coming from.

Jose said he was looking for a word from the NLP book: congruence. A student said: it is alignment. Be intentional, define your direction, and then do the actions and set up the environment and frame that are congruent with it.
Another said: it comes down to awareness, then consciousness of the variables, then decision and discipline. Once you are aware, you quickly see what is incongruent and what is congruent.
Jose said: eliminate anything that is not congruent with you: the clutter, the critics, the wrong people. Be congruent, forget the inner critic and external critics, and listen to yourself.

Jose said that the book calls specialization a way to overcome the accident of bad genetics: the more you master a specific skill, the harder it is for others to compete. If you are passionate and congruent, people feel that energy.
What is incongruent in your life today?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the daily actions that match it.
Write the daily actions that do not.
Write what you will remove: clutter, critics or the wrong people.
Write the one skill you will master.

check.q: What did a student say congruence is?
What did Jose ask about failure?
choices: Is there failure, or just process

check.q: What did Jose say the more you master a skill?
choices: The harder it is for others to compete

recap: Be congruent. Treat failure as process. Master one skill.
